subject: Q4 slate lock: temporary Dedicated GPU reservation for feature-freeze
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@artemis.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q4 slate lock: temporary Dedicated GPU reservation for feature-freeze

Hi team,

We have a high-priority feature freeze for the Q4 launch of Artemis’ pilot product, and Product needs a short, guaranteed capacity window on Dedicated to run final integration plus a coordinated canary. The ask is:

- Reserve 8 x A100-equivalent slots in the us-west dedicated pool
- Window: 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC -> 2026-10-15 23:59 UTC
- Autoscale: want a grace-period exception so these slots aren’t evicted during background autoscale churn

Why: this is a deterministic run (end-to-end validations + last-mile latency tests) that needs stable capacity for ~10k inference runs over the window. If we don’t lock, we risk flakiness during the freeze and may miss launch dates.

Attached a draft reservation sheet with preliminary token/throughput estimates (q4_slate_lock_reservation_sheet.xlsx).

Questions for infra/ops:
- Marcus/Jonas: feasibility and impacts to existing commitments (esp. Oct 4–10 high-traffic batch runs)
- What minimal autoscale policy change gives us the guarantee without blocking the pool?
- Ops runbook and rollback criteria we should follow (Jonas, can you propose?)

Dev: I’ll need you to confirm the external ask with Elena and whether Artemis is willing to accept a short credit to prioritize the window.

Proposed decision timeline: agree on approach by 08/17 so we can lock pairs by mid-September.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: q4_slate_lock_reservation_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 slate lock: temporary Dedicated GPU reservation for feature-freeze

Kimberly — thanks for the heads up. Short answer: possible, but we need to be surgical to avoid regressing other pilots in the same pool. A few immediate notes: 

- Capacity picture for us-west in early Oct is tight (several reserved pilots + marketplace demos). We can likely commit 6 slots rather than 8 without impacting SLAs.
- Autoscale exception: we can implement a "soft-lock" flag that prevents eviction for N hours after allocation; that should be sufficient for the runs and preserves overall autoscale behavior. Full hard-lock (eviction off) would be riskier.
- Tradeoff: soft-lock means we still need a buffer for bursts; recommend setting a 25% headroom reservation and allowing burst fallback to compatible model variants (cheaper quant) if needed.

Action items for me:
- I’ll run a capacity conflict check across Oct 1–15 and return a concrete slot count by EOD 08/16.
- If we go forward, I’ll create a temporary autoscale policy (soft-lock) and a capacity ticket with exact slot IDs.

Jonas — can you draft the runbook bits (health checks, eviction thresholds, rollback) and confirm oncall contact?

Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 slate lock: temporary Dedicated GPU reservation for feature-freeze

On 2026-08-15 10:03, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Capacity picture for us-west in early Oct is tight ... we can likely commit 6 slots rather than 8...

Thanks — I sketched a short runbook and attached it (q4_feature_freeze_runbook.md). High level:

- Pre-lock (T-30d): confirm slot allocation IDs, create temporary tagging (project:q4-freeze/artemis) and notify oncall rotation.
- Lock window (T0): apply soft-lock flag for slot IDs; run smoke tests (latency and throughput suites).
- Monitoring: add a dashboard with token-level latency, error rate, and queue growth thresholds. Set alerting at 2x baseline errors or >10% request queue growth sustained for 10m.
- Rollback criteria: if queue growth >25% OR error rate increases >3x baseline after 15m, we auto-release extra slots and failover to quantized variant.
- Post-window: immediate health sweep and capacity reconciliation.

Oncall: I recommend Marcus (primary) and me (secondary) during the window.

Small ask: if Marcus can confirm 6 slots we can lock to minimize impact. Also, please include the exact model variants and expected avg seq length in the reservation sheet so we can validate memory footprint.

Jonas
Sr. Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: q4_feature_freeze_runbook.md (markdown stub)
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 slate lock: temporary Dedicated GPU reservation for feature-freeze

Looping in sales context — Elena confirmed the pilot importance and is flexible on credits. Quick notes from the account side:

- Artemis is willing to take a $4k service credit against Oct billing in exchange for priority on the window.
- Procurement wants a short MSA addendum (2 paragraphs) confirming the reserved window and rollback behavior. Legal will need to review.

If we land on 6 slots + soft-lock, I can draft the customer-facing doc and run procurement in parallel. Suggest we avoid hard commitments beyond the window (keeps legal light).

Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Sales
Redwood Inference

External FYI: Elena — thanks for the fast turnaround. If this looks reasonable I’ll send the credit addendum and mirror the runbook language for the customer.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@artemis.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 slate lock: temporary Dedicated GPU reservation for feature-freeze

Thanks everyone — quick summary and decisions so we can move: 

- Agreed reservation: 6 x A100-equivalent slots in us-west
- Final window: 2026-10-02 00:00 UTC -> 2026-10-14 23:59 UTC (shifted 1 day each side to reduce overlap with other batch work)
- Autoscale: implement soft-lock flag during window; Marcus to apply and provide slot IDs by 08/18.
- Runbook & oncall: Jonas to own runbook updates and oncall pairing; Marcus primary oncall during lock.
- Customer comms: Dev to draft short addendum and credit note; Elena to confirm approval publicly by 08/19.

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Marcus: capacity conflict check & slot IDs — due 2026-08-18
- Jonas: finalize runbook & alert thresholds — due 2026-08-18
- Dev: draft addendum & credit note — due 2026-08-19
- Kimberly: lock decision and update roadmap item after confirmations — will confirm by 2026-08-20

I’ve attached an updated reservation sheet (minor edits to throughput numbers). If anyone objects to the 6-slot plan, flag today so we can re-evaluate.

Thanks — Kimberly
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
